items.title: DR Pixel: Page-Native Deep Research with Vision-Language Models
items.summary_1line: Complex documents such as scientific papers contain rich information in tables, figures, and equations; however, existing deep research (DR) agents typically reduce papers to OCR-extracted text. We instead ask whether...
items.editor_note: 심층 연구를 위해 OCR로 추출한 종이 텍스트를 페이지 수준의 시각-언어 입력으로 대체합니다.

editorial.tldr: Deep research agents are being redefined by what they read and how they search. In October, an arXiv paper proposed an iterative, state-centric agent for literature research, and another introduced a benchmark for reports centered on a source video.
editorial.whats_new: On Nov 2, DR Pixel proposed page-native deep research: vision-language models read papers as page images, rather than OCR-extracted text.
editorial.why_it_matters: Text-only retrieval pipelines drop tables, figures and equations; if your research agent ingests PDFs, the input modality is now a design choice to test.
editorial.take_for_builders: If your research agent reads PDFs, test a vision-language pass on pages with tables and equations against your OCR pipeline before trusting text-only extraction.

status.detail: Academic work is widening deep research from text search to iterative state, video sources and page images.

beats.headline: Optimist Deep Research tracks evolving understanding across literature search
beats.summary: Argues single-step retrieval plus summarization misses how an investigator's question changes.

beats.headline: A benchmark for video-centered deep research reports
beats.summary: Evaluates agents given a source video rather than a text query.

beats.headline: DR Pixel reads papers as page images with vision-language models
beats.summary: Targets tables, figures and equations lost to OCR text extraction.

open_questions: Does DR Pixel beat OCR-text baselines on figure- and table-heavy questions, and at what compute cost?
Do the video-centered and page-native benchmarks converge on a shared evaluation protocol?
Does iterative state tracking (Optimist) improve results on open-ended reports versus single-pass retrieval?
